records.question: What transaction patterns does the fraud memo flag for review?
records.answer: The fraud memo flags several transaction patterns for review or action [5]. Rule R-101 triggers on six or more card-not-present purchases within 10 minutes, which declines the sixth and later purchases and texts the customer [5]. Rule R-104 triggers on two card-present purchases more than 500 miles apart within 2 hours, which declines the second purchase and places a soft block [5]. Rule R-110 triggers on a first-ever foreign purchase over $400, requiring step-up verification in the app [5]. Rule R-117 triggers on a high-risk merchant category with an amount over $250, holding it for analyst review for up to 4 hours [5]. Rule R-122 triggers on a purchase over $1,000 within 24 hours of enrolling a new device, which declines the transaction and requires a call to Customer Care [5]. Rule R-130 triggers on three or more out-of-network ATM withdrawals in one day at different terminals, blocking ATM access for 24 hours [5].

records.question: Summarize all the rules in the fraud memo.
records.answer: The real-time card fraud rules effective March 1, 2026, include Rule R-101 Velocity, which declines the sixth and later card-not-present purchases and texts the customer when there are six or more within 10 minutes [6]. Rule R-104 Geo-jump declines the second purchase and places a soft block when there are two card-present purchases more than 500 miles apart within 2 hours [6]. Rule R-110 First foreign use requires step-up verification in the app for a first-ever foreign purchase over $400 [6]. Rule R-117 Merchant risk holds transactions for analyst review for up to 4 hours when the merchant category is high-risk and the amount is over $250 [6]. Rule R-122 New-device spend declines purchases over $1,000 within 24 hours of a new device enrolling and requires a call to Customer Care [6]. Rule R-130 ATM pattern blocks ATM access for 24 hours following 3 or more out-of-network ATM withdrawals in one day at different terminals [6].
